comment: McDowell is a very smart professor. He knows a ton about leadership and is a very old, funny dude. His grading is tough, and the homework is pretty extensive (includes lots of readings and sometimes movies). He's a great guy but is a tough grader, so just keep that in mind.

VERY smart professor. It is obvious he loves what he does and he enjoys the company of his students (when they do the readings and pay attention). Definitely not the easiest class, you might hear rumors he gives nothing higher than a C, That's false. I recommend this class if you're genuinely interested in leadership. Do the work & you'll be fine.

Dr. McDowell is the best professor I've ever had. He knows his stuff, happy to help and is a generous grader. He is as good as it gets. Though the class is not an easy A, it is very interesting and his lectures are great. He wears the best ties too! If you are interested in Jepson take his class. It really helps!

I really want to hate him because his paper topics are confusing and he grades them so hard--like worst grades I've ever gotten on writing assignments--but I can't because he's too nice and smart and helpful and he talks about his dog a lot

Gary is the best teacher ever. The comments below are very accurate. He is very tough and few people get better than the B range. I ended up with my lowest grade at Richmond, B-, but would still recommend him because he is a phenomenal teacher and knows his stuff. If you're considering Jepson, I'd take him over someone easier...you'll learn more

McDowell is honestly one of the smartest professors I have ever had. I literally sat in awe of him every class.  He is tough on writing but I improved a TON throughout the semester because of him.  If you want an A you have to earn it.
He is a hard grader and there was a lot of reading due for the class, but he wears the best ties.

Has a great sense of humor, and class discussions are very interesting. Most papers require you to cram a lot of abstract thought into 2 pages. Tests are odd in that they give you 1-3 sentences to answer abstract questions that could easily serve as essay prompts.

absolutely brilliant, great sense of humor, but sooooooo hard. I certainly recommend meeting with him outside of class. One of those class that really forces you to think. Take it, but bottom line is everybody get C's on their papers. good luck

If you do not read you will fail this class.  Strictly a lecture based classed, with very little student interaction.  He is a very smart man and very knowledgable about the subject, so he can pick up BS a mile away.  You learn a lot, but your GPA will most likely suffer.

Incredibly good teacher.  Should be a required course.  Really helps to understand where the origins of the USA are as far as beliefs, liberties, etc.  Mild conservative bias, but he has no problem with other opinions in the class.

Brilliant Prof, but a very tough grader. Take for the class not the grade.  Tons of notes, but he really has something worthwhile to say and as long as you work hard, your final grade will not totally reflect your paper grades (which will be mostly C's).  Helps to meet with him outside of class. And read, believe me it'll help.

He has a great dry sense of humor and is very intelligent. Be prepared for a lot of notetaking. He grades in a tough but fair manner (it is possible to get an A in his class if you express yourself clearly in papers). His classes are worthwhile.

He is brilliant and funny, extraordinarily hard but in a way that will make you a better student. If you don't allow yourself to be (too) intimidated by his vast knowledge and intellect, you will find him incredibly interested and helpful. Absolutely without a doubt the best professor I have had.

He knows everything about law, and he knows it, so he's the most arrogant teacher.  Most of his grades are C- and Ds.  And he finds its funny when he give crap grades.  Tells us we're learing by giving crap grades.  STAY AWAY

He is brilliant, well-connected and can teach based solely on experience if he wanted to. As smart and intimidating as he can be, he is actually very approachable and the only thing he cares more about than his own writing are his students.
